title: Undecidable quantum storage with seven elementary gates
description: Can one decide from its noise rate whether a fixed local quantum medium is an excellent memory or no scalable memory at all? We construct two six-dimensional media, one for whole-site and one for independent single-qubit depolarization, for which this distinction is undecidable. Both use only X, H, CNOT, Toffoli, reset, dephasing and identity, with noise after every elementary layer. Computable disjoint rational windows select universal-machine inputs: above a computable size threshold, nonhalting preserves a reference-entangled qubit with fidelity at least 15/16 through exponentially many rounds, while halting destroys every encoding after a time uniform in size and rate. We also obtain stretched-exponential storage on the undecidable windows in four dimensions under whole-site noise, using a static cap and a folded concatenated code with a periodic classical calendar. Its fixed positive exponent is below 0.0002 and astronomically small; the bound beats a given polynomial only at astronomically large sizes. One total computable encoder serves all guaranteed times and rates in each window. For the six-dimensional media we also give a coarse lifetime upper bound and Π⁰₁-complete certification by exact finite tests; the three-dimensional construction retains its sharp linear scale. All interactions have fixed, very large range, and the windows lie below astronomically small rate caps. The Bell-sharing bound and conditional window certification are verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib. Every finite sample eventually forgets; what is undecidable is how useful storage time grows with size.
notes: Preprint. It has not been peer reviewed. Version 2.1.0 updates version 2.0.0 (10.5281/zenodo.24269020). New: Theorem D, stretched-exponential qubit storage exp(c_4 L^alpha_4) on the undecidable noise windows for a fixed seven-gate medium on Z^4 under whole-site depolarization after every layer, with every-encoding destruction on halting windows (alpha_4 < 2*10^-4; no lifetime upper bound for this medium); and Lean 4 verification of the Bell-sharing bound (Lemma 6.6) and of the conditional window certification (Theorem G.1). Theorems A and B and Proposition 9.8 are unchanged. The authors have not independently verified the mathematical arguments; the work used a combination of AI models with cross-developer checks.
